collection: NCEE original reading and contextual word relationships
note: 24 Verbal Aptitude and 24 English Studies drafts. Six original reading stimuli. Primary 6 suitability is provisional from historical NERDC reference; official 2026 components are confirmed separately. Four-option MCQ is an author practice choice. These receptive items do not assess writing, speaking or a complete NCEE paper. All academic review pending.

questions.subject: English Studies
questions.learningObjective: Explain character behaviour and select a future action supported by a story.
questions.prompt: Why does Nnenna check the names with the artists before reporting the error?
options: To make sure her report is correct.
To choose which drawing should win.
To make the visitors arrive later.
To discover which artist is older.
questions.answer: To make sure her report is correct.
questions.explanation: Checking with the artists gives evidence for the correction; the story gives no competition or age enquiry.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one practice mark are author choices; official NCEE option count and marking blueprint remain unverified.
questions.passage: On the morning of the class exhibition, Nnenna noticed that the labels on two drawings had been exchanged. The visitors were due soon. Her friend suggested leaving them because the teacher might blame the person who reported the mistake. Nnenna checked the names with the two artists, then told the teacher what she had found. She did not guess who had moved the labels. The teacher thanked her and asked her to help put them right. Later, a visitor praised a drawing and read the correct artist’s name aloud. Nnenna smiled and returned to arranging the display.

options: The microphone fails before his performance.

questions.answer: The microphone fails before his performance.
questions.explanation: The equipment failure is explicitly the unexpected problem.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one practice mark are author choices; official NCEE option count and marking blueprint remain unverified.
questions.passage: Musa had practised a poem for the school assembly. Just before his turn, the microphone stopped working. He looked towards the back row and took a breath. Instead of rushing through the poem, he faced the audience and spoke more clearly, pausing between the lines. Afterwards, his younger cousin said she had heard every word. Musa thanked the teacher who had advised him to practise without equipment as well as with it. He still hoped the microphone would be repaired, but he decided to keep rehearsing both ways.

questions.subject: English Studies
questions.learningObjective: Locate and interpret information in a short factual text or chart.
questions.prompt: What happens before volunteers begin strengthening a cover?
options: A teacher checks whether it can be repaired.
The records are removed from the school.
Loose pages are sold to visitors.
questions.answer: A teacher checks whether it can be repaired.
questions.explanation: The teacher checks suitability before approving cover repairs.
questions.practiceFormatNote: Four options and one practice mark are author choices; official NCEE option count and marking blueprint remain unverified.
questions.passage: A school introduced a repair table for torn book covers. Pupils first placed a slip inside each book to describe the damage. A teacher checked whether a cover could be repaired and kept books with loose pages for separate attention. Volunteers used suitable paper and tape to strengthen the covers approved for repair. They recorded which books were ready before returning them to the shelves. The project did not make every book look new, but it made many damaged covers firm enough for continued use. The class kept the records so it could see which repairs lasted.

questions.passage: At a fictional school garden, the pupils use a weekly task chart. The chart lists Monday: inspect paths; Tuesday: remove dry leaves from paths; Wednesday: check labels; Thursday: record plant growth; Friday: review unfinished jobs. The class does not water simply because a day has a particular name. A teacher checks the soil before deciding whether water is needed. When rain interrupts an outdoor task, the pupils note what remains unfinished. Friday’s review helps the class decide what to carry forward rather than pretending that every planned job was completed.
